subject: maths
title: Statistical Methods
introductionText:
Term 1 · Statistics
Statistical Methods
The Big Idea: When we collect lots of information, we sort it and show it as a picture — a
list, a table, a pictogram or a block graph — so we can answer questions just by looking.
Say It Like This
Read aloud
"Let's find out which fruit our family likes best. First we ask everyone and write a list. Then
we draw one little picture for each person, in rows. That is a pictogram. The longest row is
the favourite. A block graph is the same idea, but we colour one square for each person,
one on top of the other."
Watch Out For
The slip almost every child makes
Pictures of different sizes. If the banana pictures are drawn big and the apple pictures
small, the banana row looks longer even with fewer bananas. Every picture must be the
same size, lined up from the same starting line — just like lining up pencils to compare
them.
Guessing from height instead of counting. In a block graph, count the blocks. Two
columns that look "about the same" may differ by one.
Try It at Home
Game 1 — The family fruit vote (10 minutes)
Ask everyone at home (and grandparents on the phone): "Which fruit do you like best?"
Put a real fruit (or a sticky note) on the table for each answer, in rows, starting from the
edge of the table. Before counting, ask him: "Which row do you think is longest?" Then
count each row.
Game 2 — Sorting in a table (5 minutes)
Tip a handful of his toys on the floor. Make a two-column table on paper: red / not red.
He puts each toy in the right column. Then re-sort the same toys a new way: has wheels /
no wheels. Same toys, new groups!
Our favourite fruit (pictogram) The same, as a block graph

apple banana orange mango
Count each row of the pictogram with him, then find the same number of blocks in the graph. Ask: which
shows the favourite more clearly?
More examples to talk about
• Ten people voted: 4 + 2 + 3 + 1 = 10. Adding all the rows tells you how many people
were asked.
• A table is a quick way to write the same information with numbers instead of pictures.
• A Carroll diagram is a table with two boxes, like red and not red. Every toy fits in exactly
one box.
• Tricky: if nobody picks grapes, the grape row is empty — but it still has a row, showing
zero.
• Class weather charts and votes for a class name are real pictograms.
Key Words
list table pictogram block graph sort Carroll diagram most least

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
Five children said their favourite pet: Sara – cat, Omar – dog, Laila – cat, Adam – fish,
Nour – cat. Fill in the table.
cat dog fish
Ask 4 people their favourite colour. Draw a pictogram with one circle for each person.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Four circles in total, same size, lined up in rows by colour.

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
In our pictogram, each picture stands for...
( nobody ) ( one person ) ( two people )

The longest row in a pictogram shows the...
( most ) ( first ) ( least )

A block graph is made of...
( only words ) ( only circles ) ( blocks (squares) )

In the picture above, how many people chose orange?
( 4 ) ( 3 ) ( 2 )

Pictures in a pictogram should be...
( anywhere on the page ) ( the same size and lined up ) ( all different sizes )
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: the same size and lined up
